info.name: AI Journal Platform - Full API Suite
info.description:
Complete, accurate collection covering every real endpoint exposed through the gateway (localhost:8080) as of this repo's current `main` branch (post-Phase 22). Replaces the previous 3 overlapping/stale collections (root `AI_Journal_Platform.postman_collection.json` and 2 near-duplicates under `docs/`), none of which reflected MFA, password reset, email verification, admin, or the current notification/recommendation/analytics endpoints.

Quick start: run **Register User**, then **Login User** (auto-saves `accessToken`/`refreshToken`/`userId` as collection variables via its test script) - every other request inherits the bearer token automatically. If the account has MFA enabled, Login returns a challenge instead of tokens; run **Verify MFA Challenge** next using the code from an authenticator app seeded via **Setup MFA**.

Two endpoints in the Notifications folder (`POST /send-email`, `POST /notifications`) are `ROLE_SYSTEM`-only and will correctly 403 with a normal user's JWT - included for API-contract completeness, not because a client should call them directly.

item.name: 1. Auth Service
item.description: Registration, login (incl. MFA challenge), token refresh, password management, and email verification. All public except /me, /password, /mfa/*, /verify-email*.

request.description: Creates an account with emailVerified=false and mfaEnabled=false. Auto-saves the issued tokens.
Returns AuthResponse{accessToken,refreshToken,userId} for a normal account, or MfaChallengeResponse{mfaRequired:true,challengeToken} if the account has MFA enabled.
Completes login after a Login response with mfaRequired:true. Send either `code` (TOTP) or `recoveryCode`, never both.
Rotates the refresh token; re-checks the account is still enabled.
Revokes the given refresh token.
Returns id, username, email, fullName, roles, mfaEnabled, emailVerified.
Requires the current password. Revokes all existing refresh tokens on success.
Always returns the same generic message regardless of whether the email is registered (enumeration-safe). Sends a real reset code via email (MailHog in dev).
Single-use code from the forgot-password email. Revokes all existing refresh tokens on success.
Returns {mfaEnabled}.
Generates and persists a TOTP secret (mfaEnabled stays false until Enable MFA confirms it). Returns {secret, otpAuthUri} for QR-code enrollment.
Confirms setup with a real 6-digit code from an authenticator app seeded with Setup MFA's secret. Returns 10 recovery codes once, in plaintext.
Requires both the current password and a valid code as a safety check.
Code from the verification email sent at registration. Idempotent no-op if already verified.
Generates and sends a fresh code, invalidating any earlier one. 400s if already verified.

item.name: 2. Admin (Auth Service)
item.description: hasRole('ADMIN')-gated user management. The seeded dev bootstrap admin is admin/AdminBootstrap123! (rotate before any real deployment).

request.description: Paginated UserSummaryResponse list.
ROLE_USER is always retained server-side regardless of what's sent. Rejects self-demotion from ADMIN.
Disabling also revokes all of that user's refresh tokens. Rejects self-disable.

item.name: 3. Journal Service
item.description: CRUD + pin/favorite/archive + soft (trash) and permanent delete. Content is encrypted at rest (AES/GCM) and transparently decrypted in every response here.

request.description: Auto-saves the created id. Untitled/blank title defaults to 'Untitled Journal Entry'; mood defaults per Journal.mood's field initializer (see root CLAUDE.md's documented defaulting quirk).
Excludes soft-deleted (trashed) entries via @SQLRestriction.
Any field omitted (e.g. content) keeps its existing value rather than being overwritten with null.
Moves to trash (is_deleted=true) - recoverable in principle, not exposed via a restore endpoint today.
Genuinely removes the row (bypasses the soft-delete restriction via native SQL - Phase 22 fix). Works whether or not the journal was trashed first.

item.name: 4. AI Features (ai-service)
item.description: Backed by python-ai-service (Flask). Falls back to a lightweight deterministic mock strategy if the Flask backend is unreachable (ai.provider=mock).

request.description: Also persists a MoodHistory row when journalId is a real, owned journal.

item.name: 5. Search Service
item.description: Elasticsearch-backed, userId-scoped. `query`/`mood`/`tag` are independently optional and combinable on the fulltext endpoint.

request.description: Fuzzy, relevance-ranked full-text search across title/content - not ML-embedding-based semantic search.

item.name: 6. User Profile & Preferences
item.description: Profile/preferences rows are created lazily (get-or-create) on first GET.

request.description: All 5 fields are overwritten unconditionally - send the full shape, not a partial patch.
Deletes profile+preferences rows if they exist (Phase 22 fix - no longer crashes for a never-touched-profile user).

item.name: 7. Recommendation Service
item.description: Mood-aware curated (non-LLM) content, real caller: Mindora's Dashboard.

request.description: If currentMood is omitted, it's computed from the caller's 5 most recent real journal entries (forwards this request's own Authorization header to journal-service).
category is genuinely honored (GRATITUDE/REFLECTION/GOALS each return distinct content, Phase 22 fix) - unrecognized/omitted falls back to a default bucket.

item.name: 8. Analytics Service
item.description: Computed live from the caller's real journal history (up to the most recent 500 entries) - fetches journal-service the same way recommendation-service does.

request.description: totalWordsWritten, mostCommonEmotions, topTopics, mostProductiveDays, writingFrequency, currentStreakDays, longestStreakDays. No mostMentionedPeople/Places - deliberately dropped rather than faked (no NER infra).

item.name: 9. Notifications
item.description: GET/read-all/device-token are for the caller's own data. POST / and /send-email are ROLE_SYSTEM-only (403 with a normal user JWT) - included for contract completeness.

request.description: Expect 403 unless the bearer token carries ROLE_SYSTEM - real callers mint a short-lived internal token themselves (auth-service), never a normal user JWT.
Expect 403 with a normal user JWT - same restriction and reasoning as Send Email.

item.name: 10. File Attachments
item.description: Local-disk storage today (no S3). Download rejects any path not prefixed with the caller's own user-{userId}/.

request.description: Stores under user-{{userId}}/. Response includes the real storedPath to use in Download File.
